items.item_text: Current CA licensure as a Psychologist
Doctoral degree in Clinical Psychology, Counseling Psychology, or related field
Experience providing evidence-based treatment for individuals with psychotic disorders, schizophrenia spectrum disorders, or other serious mental illnesses
Experience working within academic medical centers, community health programs, or specialty psychosis programs
Experience providing crisis intervention, treatment coordination, and multidisciplinary behavioral health services

Our Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior is seeking to hire a limited part-time Psychologist to join the UCLA Psychosis Clinic. The Psychosis Clinic provide comprehensive, recovery-oriented services designed to help individuals achieve stability, independence, and meaningful participation in their communities. Through a multidisciplinary treatment approach, the clinic integrates evidence-based psychotherapy, family support, psycho-education, crisis intervention, vocational services, educational support, and coordinated psychiatric care. Key responsibilities:
Provide evidence-based assessment and therapeutic interventions for individuals with psychotic disorders and serious mental illness
Facilitate individual and group psychotherapy, psychoeducation, and supportive interventions
Deliver crisis intervention and collaborate with psychiatrists and treatment team members regarding patient care needs and treatment planning
Serve as liaison among patients, families, community providers, housing resources, educational programs, and vocational support services
Provide consultation, teaching, and clinical guidance to psychology trainees and interdisciplinary team members
Participate in Supported Employment and Education (SEE) services utilizing the Individual Placement and Support (IPS) model to help patients pursue educational and vocational goals
Maintain clinical documentation in accordance with organizational and regulatory requirements, including HIPAA standards
Please note: this is a limited appointment that may convert to career
Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across disciplines
Familiarity with Supported Employment and Education (SEE) and/or the Individual Placement and Support (IPS) model
Knowledge of HIPAA regulations and clinical documentation standard
